reason: The variety has short-elliptic leaves '(not broadly obovate)'. A negated obovate shape on the leaf says what the flora says.
Branchlets are 'blackish brown ... when old'. Branch + color brown with the stage slot old (PATO_0000308) matches. 'Blackish brown' falls under brown.
'Summer-green' means the fronds are green in summer and die back in winter, i.e. deciduous. Whole plant + deciduous (plant) is a fair reading.
The inflorescence is 'densely many-flowered'. Flower present, with inflorescence as the container and count word 'many', matches.
The sterile lemma encloses a palea and an 'abortive perfect flower'. Flower + abortive (FLOPO_0991250) matches.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the adaxial leaf surface (leaf adaxial trichome PO_0025211); color brown
fix: A color word just before a hair term ('brownish puberulous', 'rust-brown villous', 'whitish pubescent') gives the color of the hairs, not of the surface. Put the color on the trichome of that surface and the pilosity on the surface.

Female spikes '(15-)25-60 x 4-6 mm'. Length 25-60 mm, lower extreme 15 and the female state slot are all right.

fix: 'Sparsely hirsute adaxially, sparsely pubescent ... abaxially': a side adverb (adaxially/abaxially) after a hair term limits it to that surface. Keep the side, as done for A01935.

fix: In Liliaceae (Nomocharis, Lilium, Fritillaria) 'outer ones / inner ones' refer to tepals. Resolve 'ones' to the perianth term that introduces the passage, not to petal.

fix: 'Prickles' (Rosa, Rubus) are outgrowths of the epidermis and cortex, not modified shoots. Map 'prickle(s)' to PO prickle, never to thorn.

target: bract shape ellipsoid (PATO_0001866) + bract apex shape acuminate (PATO_0002228)
fix: A hyphen joining an outline term and an apex term ('ellipsoid-acuminate', 'ovate-acuminate', 'oblong-obtuse') means an outline with that apex, not a range between two shapes. Split into the outline on the part and the apex term on the part's apex.

Lateral sepals 'obovate or elliptic'. The lateral position is missing, but the dorsal sepal is also obovate, so 'sepal obovate or elliptic' is still true. Adding the position would be better.

'Filaments subequalling anthers': filament length about equal to anther length, ratio about 1. The 'sub' (nearly) is approximate but the relation is right.

target: claw of banner petal, adaxial (inner) surface, distal part; tomentose

fix: Qualities defined by how the base looks (clawed, and also cuneate or cordate when given as 'base X') belong on the whole organ or follow the base-shape pattern. Moving them onto 'petal base' makes the base itself clawed, which is wrong.
